correctness.rationale: The normalized four-child contrast h_(v,a)=2^j chi_a has squared mass one on its length-j cylinder; 1+3 sum_{j<d}4^j=4^d verifies completeness. For a fixed evaluation leaf the signed local row is one of exactly eight ±(3,-1,-1,-1) Walsh permutations. Disjoint sibling subcylinders and the continuation child yield the exact Bellman recurrence for the absolute kernel's L1 mass. The interval |u|≤1 is invariant; assuming F_(k−1)=A+B|u|, exact comparison of on-child versus sibling-exception branches gives (1−B)(1−|u|)/2≥0. Thus B_k=(1+B_(k−1))/4, A_k=A_(k−1)+(5+B_(k−1))/4, producing U_d=4d/3+5/9+4/(9·4^d), including d=0. The branch strictness/ties give ancestral optimizer counts 4 (d=1), 16·3^(d−2) (d≥2), all terminal leaves are symmetric, and kernel-sign inputs attain row sums. Separately reconstructing binary recursion yields the same number at depth 2d without an operator-family equivalence. Independent rational Bellman computation d=0..6, plus inspected verify.py local sign-class and brute path code, corroborates but does not replace the all-depth induction.

value.rationale: Sharp finite-depth unconditionality in L∞ is a natural invariant of a complete four-child Haar dictionary. The equality with 2d binary generations is a non-obvious rigidity across inequivalent local sign classes, and the exact optimizer count resolves meaningful extremal structure at every depth. These are reusable structural endpoint facts, not a renamed dyadic theorem or an arbitrary finite table.

limitations: Only complete, uniform, real four-child Walsh/Hadamard Haar generations; no rotated contrasts, biased masses, 0/1 suppression, arbitrary finite trees.
